environment.description: Kubernetes pod running on GKE Autopilot with the following runtime constraints: (1) Pod securityContext sets fsGroup=65534 and runAsNonRoot with readOnlyRootFilesystem=true, with a dedicated emptyDir volume mounted at /tmp with medium=Memory and sizeLimit=10Mi — this emptyDir is private to the pod's mount namespace so no other process outside the pod can access it. (2) The GKE node pool runs gVisor (runsc) as the OCI runtime via RuntimeClass 'gvisor', which interposes all syscalls including symlink/rename through its Sentry component, preventing cross-namespace symlink resolution and enforcing O_NOFOLLOW semantics on all file creation syscalls in /tmp. (3) NetworkPolicy restricts egress to only the Kubernetes DNS service and the internal API, meaning even if the temp file were tampered with and the rendered HTML modified, the integrity attribute on the script tag would fail validation since the CDN script cannot be replaced — but more critically, no attacker process can coexist in the pod's mount namespace to race the symlink.
